correctness.rationale: Universal proof reconstructed: for normalized unconditional Schauder E not equal to coordinate ell1, finite-support density yields positive a with ||a||=1<sum a_i. Hahn--Banach gives f0 norming a; lattice modulus f=|f0| is positive with ||f||=f(a)=1, and some a_i>0 has f(e_i)<1. The sign isometry fixing i and negating all other basis coordinates gives x=(Sa,0), F=(S*f,1), ||x||=||F||=F(x)=1. The positive parts satisfy x+=(a_i e_i,0), F+=(f_i e_i*,1), ||F+||=1 and F+(x+)=a_i f_i<a_i=||F+||||x+||. Coordinate functionals determine the E* lattice parts because finite spans are dense. Conversely, if every finite-support norm is ell1 additive, completion E=ell1, X=ell1 on the enlarged index set; equality in Holder forces each F_j=sign x_j on occupied coordinates, so HNAp holds for both Jordan parts, including zero parts and all normalized/scaled pairs.
residual_risks: Finite examples cannot establish the universal finite/countably infinite Schauder claim; analytic Hahn--Banach and basis-density argument does.
The theorem is restricted to real coordinate Banach lattices with normalized 1-unconditional Schauder bases and one scalar l1 summand; no claim for atomless or non-Schauder coordinate systems.

originality.rationale: The closest sound original source, arXiv:2106.05935v1, proves two-dimensional HNAp and exhibits one three-dimensional failure, not an iff classification over all normalized 1-unconditional Schauder Banach sequence lattices. Its L1 sufficiency is known and explicitly credited. Independent result-index searches return the assigned published record as a self-match but no separate valid universal extension result. An apparently encompassing 2026 Proposition 4.1 is mathematically false: its asserted universal Jordan upper bound is contradicted by the original 2021 octagonal example (sum 5/4>1), so it cannot supply a valid prior proof of this classification. AHSp and operator BPBp sums treat a distinct property. Best-of-knowledge originality PASS, not proof of historical priority.
residual_risks: An older non-indexed characterization of scalar-l1 stability of Jordan-part HNAp under abstract AL-space terminology might exist; internet and semantic results are not complete.
The 2026 Moraa--Okelo--Omoke Proposition 4.1 has a printed false general assertion; no inference about the full remainder of that paper or any corrected future version is made.
The assigned record already appears in Resultary; its chronology relative to other October-11 records is not established, and this self-match is excluded as separate historical priority evidence.

value.rationale: The exact one-scalar-summand HNAp permanence question is natural because the introducing paper proves every 2D absolute norm has HNAp but constructs one failing 3D scalar-l1 extension. The new iff identifies the precise geometric obstruction: norm nonadditivity on disjoint positive coordinates. It classifies every finite/countable normalized unconditional Schauder sequence lattice, including Euclidean and supremum planes, and explains failure by a uniform norming pair. A structural all-space boundary is a meaningful independent mathematical fact; it is neither an arbitrary slice nor a table recomputation. Significance is restricted to HNAp and this normed/direct-sum class.
residual_risks: No classification is asserted for arbitrary non-atomic Banach lattices or general absolute direct sums.
A concise proof and elementary functional analysis do not by themselves certify priority; value follows from resolving a motivated universal permanence classification.

final_claim: For a real Banach sequence lattice E with a finite or countably infinite normalized 1-unconditional Schauder basis and coordinate order, X=E⊕_1 R has hereditary norm-attaining property in the Acosta--Soleimani sense exactly when every finitely supported u has ||u||=sum_i|u_i| (equivalently E is coordinatewise ell1). Non-ell1 E admits a norming pair violating the positive-part equality; ell1 suffices. No atomless, general absolute-sum or positive-functional BPBp classification is claimed.
limitations: The claim uses real scalars, a finite/countably infinite normalized 1-unconditional Schauder basis and the coordinatewise order.
Finite rational checks corroborate but do not prove all countable-dimensional Banach-lattice cases.
